s1.syndrome_frame: febrile neutropenic patient with cutaneous lesions and evidence of disseminated infection
salient_findings: vesicles with erythematous base on the skin
filamentous bacilli with septa on microscopic examination
key_facts: female infant with history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
became febrile 17 days after last day of chemotherapy
neutropenic at the time of fever
had an indwelling catheter
vesicles observed on lower back and left thigh
tissue and blood cultures were obtained
punch biopsy of vesicle on lower back was performed
microscopic examination showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis
numerous filamentous bacilli with septa on microscopic examination
gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods
periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for HSV and VZV were negative
CT scan showed lesions in the liver and brain

shortlist.label: Nocardia asteroides infection
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods and microscopic examination showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa

shortlist.label: Nocardia brasiliensis infection
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of vesicles with an erythematous base and laboratory findings of gram-variable rods and filamentous bacilli are consistent with Nocardia infection

shortlist.label: Nocardia farcinica infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's immunocompromised state and presence of an indwelling catheter increase the risk for Nocardia infection

shortlist.label: Nocardia nova infection
shortlist.why_kept: Disseminated infection with lesions in the liver and brain is consistent with Nocardia infection

shortlist.label: Nocardia transvalensis infection
shortlist.why_kept: Microscopic examination findings and negative PCR testing for HSV and VZV make Nocardia infection a plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of filamentous bacilli with septa and gram-variable rods in the microscopic examination, along with the clinical presentation of vesicles and the patient's immunocompromised state, are consistent with Nocardia infection. Nocardia asteroides is a common cause of infection in immunocompromised patients, particularly those with a history of cancer and neutropenia.

rejected.label: Nocardia brasiliensis infection
rejected.why: Nocardia brasiliensis is more commonly associated with mycetoma, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Nocardia farcinica infection
rejected.why: Nocardia farcinica is less common than Nocardia asteroides and not as frequently associated with the described clinical presentation

rejected.label: Nocardia nova infection
rejected.why: Nocardia nova is less common and not as well-documented in the literature as Nocardia asteroides

rejected.label: Nocardia transvalensis infection
rejected.why: Nocardia transvalensis is less common and not as frequently associated with the described clinical presentation
